title: Horizon-bounded slew-rate with credit-leasing autoscale policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a new autoscaling policy for Dedicated fleets that combines a horizon-bounded slew-rate limiter with a tenant credit-leasing mechanism. The goal is to provide predictable throughput guarantees while allowing short, controlled bursts without destabilizing fleet capacity or causing cost runaway. This ticket covers policy design, config surface, runtime hooks, control-plane storage for credits, local simulator, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Policy config exposes: min_replicas, max_replicas, max_scale_per_minute, horizon_seconds, credit_leasing_window, credit_repayment_rate, emergency_fallback_model
Sustained workload tests show <1% additional SLA misses compared to baseline while reducing cost of overprovisioning by >=15% on representative traces
Simulator and e2e smoke tests validate credit accounting across restarts and failover
Console shows per-tenant credit balance, lease events, and a visualization of horizon-bounded scale decisions
Canary rollout plan and rollback procedure documented and rehearsed
design_notes: Key ideas: 1) Horizon-bounded slew-rate: enforce a maximum aggregated scale delta over a sliding window (horizon_seconds) to prevent rapid oscillation. 2) Credit-leasing: tenants accumulate steady-state headroom credits when underutilized and may 'lease' those credits for short bursts. Leases are repaid over a configurable repayment window with decay, and the control plane enforces tenant-level credit caps. 3) Hybrid decision rule: base target = percentile throughput target (p95 tokens/sec or request/sec) mapped to replica count; allow temporary exceedance up to credit balance; otherwise enforce slew cap. 4) Safety fences: per-tenant max replicas, global fleet budget guard, cost budget alarms, and immediate fallback to cheaper model variant on sustained overload. 5) Observability: emit "scale_intent", "credit_leased", "credit_repayment", and "horizon_violation" events.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize config schema and API with PM + Prod Infra
Week 2: Implement config parsing and credit ledger storage in control plane (sharded by tenant)
Week 3: Implement decision function and horizon-slew limiter in scaler component; add unit tests
Week 4: Build local simulator and run representative workload traces to tune parameters
Week 5: Integrate telemetry events and dashboard panels in Console
Week 6: Canary rollout (10% tenants) with extended logging and rollback hooks
Week 7: Collect metrics, iterate, and expand rollout to 50% then GA
rollout_plan: Start with non-critical tenants and test groups. Canary at 10% for 72 hours with strict monitoring of p95 latency, error rate, and credit repayment anomalies. If >0.5% increase in p95 or any sustained credit-negative drift (>2x expected), roll back within 30 minutes. Gradually increase to 50% for one week before GA. Critical tenants and enterprise contracts will remain on the legacy autoscaler until manual opt-in.
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit arithmetic, lease/repay edge cases, and persistence across restarts
Simulator runs with 100 synthetic traces including bursty tails, diurnal patterns, and failover scenarios
Integration tests exercising fallback to cheaper model when global budget breached
Chaos test: control-plane restart and verify idempotent credit reconciliation
Load test: verify global fleet constraints and embedded cooldowns under 2x expected peak
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: per-tenant credit balance, lease rate, repayment rate, horizon-violations
SLO delta monitor: compare canary vs baseline p95 and error-rate (auto-fail if delta > configured)
